primary_diagnosis_treated: End-stage diabetic nephropathy (ESRD) secondary to long‑standing diabetes

medications.dose: 1.25 mg orally once daily, titrate by 1.25 mg every 2–4 weeks to max 10 mg daily as tolerated
medications.duration: Lifelong — review annually and after each titration step
medications.purpose: Renoprotective and antihypertensive therapy for CKD with proteinuria
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends ACE‑I for CKD with ACR ≥30 mg/mmol or hypertension; monitor creatinine and potassium after 1–2 weeks

medications.dose: 20 mg orally once daily in the evening
medications.purpose: Cardiovascular risk reduction in CKD (CVD risk equivalent)
medications.nice_justification: NG203 states all CKD patients should receive a statin for CV risk reduction

medications.dose: 500 mg IV over 15 minutes (repeat after iron studies, usually 2–4 weeks later if needed)
medications.duration: Single dose; repeat as required based on ferritin/TSAT
medications.purpose: Correct iron deficiency before ESA therapy in anaemia of CKD
medications.nice_justification: NG107 recommends IV iron for iron deficiency (ferritin <200 µg/L or TSAT <20%) in CKD

medications.dose: 5,000 IU subcutaneously once weekly (adjust to maintain Hb 100–120 g/L)
medications.duration: Until Hb 100–120 g/L achieved, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Treat symptomatic anaemia of CKD after iron repletion
medications.nice_justification: NG107 advises ESA for CKD anaemia (Hb <100 g/L) after iron stores are corrected

medications.duration: Until corrected calcium <2.6 mmol/L and phosphate target achieved, then review every 3 months
medications.purpose: Manage secondary hyperparathyroidism / vitamin D deficiency in CKD‑MBD
medications.nice_justification: NG107 recommends vitamin D analogues for CKD‑MBD when 25‑OH‑vit D is low or PTH elevated

medications.dose: 800 mg orally with each main meal (3 times daily)
medications.duration: Lifelong — monitor phosphate every 3 months and adjust dose
medications.nice_justification: NG107 advises phosphate binders for phosphate >1.5 mmol/L; sevelamer avoids calcium load

medications.dose: 5 mg orally once daily (increase to 10 mg if needed)
medications.purpose: Additional antihypertensive if target <130/80 mmHg not reached on ACE‑I alone
medications.nice_justification: NG203 recommends adding CCB when BP remains uncontrolled despite ACE‑I/ARB

contraindications.reason: eGFR 6 mL/min/1.73 m² (<30) – high risk of lactic acidosis
contraindications.alternative: None; avoid metformin in advanced CKD

contraindications.reason: Accelerate CKD progression and cause fluid retention
Increased risk of hyperkalaemia and acute kidney injury
NICE TA775 limits use to eGFR ≥20 mL/min/1.73 m²; patient eGFR 6
contraindications.alternative: No SGLT2 inhibitor; rely on ACE‑I for renoprotection

assumptions_warnings: Baseline serum potassium, calcium, phosphate, PTH, and bicarbonate not provided – required before initiating ACE‑I, vitamin D analogue, and phosphate binder.
Hemoglobin, ferritin, and transferrin saturation not available – iron study needed before ESA.
Blood pressure reading not supplied – target <130/80 mmHg will guide titration of Ramipril and need for Amlodipine.
Liver function tests not provided – needed before starting atorvastatin.
Allergy status unknown – verify no ACE‑I, statin, or iron preparation allergies before prescribing.
Current antiplatelet/anticoagulant therapy not listed – assess bleeding risk given occult GI bleed and ESA use.
treatment_summary: Start renoprotective ACE‑I (Ramipril) and statin (Atorvastatin) for CKD and cardiovascular risk. Correct iron deficiency with IV ferric carboxymaltose, then initiate ESA (Epoetin alfa) if Hb remains <100 g/L. Manage CKD‑MBD with alfacalcidol and sevelamer, adjusting based on calcium, phosphate, and PTH results. Add amlodipine if BP target is not met on ACE‑I alone. Avoid metformin, chronic NSAIDs, dual RAAS blockade, and SGLT2 inhibitors due to eGFR 6. Monitor labs and BP per NICE NG203/NG107 recommendations and review medications regularly.
